clue.text: Aftershave contracts boxer that's tough

parts.note: Brut is a well-known brand of aftershave

indicators.note: contracts says the boxer's name is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer signs a sponsorship deal with an aftershave brand, which seems a hard-nosed business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a verb about deals, but it shortens ALI to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brutal is harsh and unyielding, a near synonym of tough.

clue.text: So a heartless Led Zeppelin IV tour's awful — will you attend?

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged
heartless means the middle letter of the word Led is removed

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter of the fodder here

explanation.surface: A fan complains that a Led Zeppelin tour promoting their fourth album lacked soul and was dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Led loses its middle E to give LD; the rest of the fodder is taken as written. The answer is the French phrase behind RSVP on invitations.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase printed as RSVP on invitations asks the guest to reply about coming, so it amounts to a request for attendance.

clue.text: Snack done perfectly that is providing sandwich for son

indicators.note: sandwich for means the letter for son is placed between other letters

parts.note: done to a T means done exactly right
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A recipe note praising a perfectly made snack that a son is given in a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' is a link word; 'sandwich' is the container signal, misleadingly in a food clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sandwich is a familiar light snack, known by this informal British name.

clue.text: Composition of Page/Plant — disc in an artwork

indicators.note: composition here means putting the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Led Zeppelin album sleeve is described: a record by Jimmy Page and Robert Plant set within a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: Page and Plant are Led Zeppelin's guitarist and singer; 'Composition' suggests music but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of countryside scenery is a type of artwork, the genre of Constable and Turner.

clue.text: See 4
Balls trapped in underwear — they split hairs

indicators.note: trapped in says one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: pants is the British word for underpants
Ed Balls is a British Labour politician, so Balls points to Ed

explanation.surface: A painful underwear mishap, followed by a remark about fussy people.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a former UK Labour minister; his surname is the misleading word, with the cheeky surface image.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants fuss over tiny distinctions, which is what splitting hairs means.

clue.text: Urge forward, one to mark short footballer …

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is an abbreviation for mark, the former German currency

indicators.note: short means the footballer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Pele, the Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A coach encourages a player, while someone marks a short footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push something onward, a synonym of urging forward.

clue.text: … yet unusually hurt tackling nothing?

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the rearranged letters surround the piece for nothing
unusually signals the letters of hurt are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement
SFA, sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a footballer oddly unhurt after a tackle that came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the footballer in 6; 'tackling' means gripping, so the jumbled 'hurt' wraps the slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus far means up to now, which is the sense of yet in 'not yet'.

clue.text: Want skinny rat? Watch catcher, ultimately, six feet under collecting equipment for sewer

parts.note: to want is to need
skinny means lean

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the word for buried surrounds the final letters

parts.note: six feet under is an idiom for buried, so dead

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A rambling description of a thin rat, a watch, a rat-catcher and a burial, ending with sewer gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, fitting the rat, but means one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress or tailor, one who sews, works with this pair of tools.

clue.text: Twisted end of cap — fresh sardine packaging

indicators.note: packaging means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters enclose the letter from cap
fresh signals the letters of sardine are made anew

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of cap

explanation.surface: A tin of fresh sardines with its cap bent at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packaging' puts P inside SRAINED, the anagram of SARDINE from 'fresh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprained ankle is one that has been wrenched, so sprained means twisted.

clue.text: Dried fruit shapes

definitions.meaning: trims or forms a plant by cutting back

explanation.definitionFit: The word means dried plums as a noun and, as a verb, cuts back or forms a hedge or tree.

clue.text: Picked stuff that's green and returned bags?

indicators.note: returned means the word for bags is read backwards

parts.note: bags of something means lots, tons

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether green produce was picked and the bags brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked stuff that's green' suggests vegetables, but it is what you pick from your nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal mucus, often green, is what someone picks from their nose, a grim cryptic description.

clue.text: Two records, one after the other

parts.note: a single is a record with one track
a file is a record kept on paper or computer

explanation.surface: Two records played one straight after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in this way means in a line, each person behind another.

clue.text: Some strange Nevada city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that some city in Nevada is a strange place.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a Swiss city on its lake, home to many international bodies.

clue.text: Casting TV hit as a weary one gets number

indicators.note: casting means throwing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Casting a weary TV actor in a hit show earns them a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' means a song, not a figure; the answer is Led Zeppelin's most famous song.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a piece of music, and this is a celebrated rock song.

clue.text: Sugar maybe taking one part of 7 tree

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the name contains the numeral

parts.note: Alan Sugar, the British businessman of The Apprentice, so Sugar gives Alan
I is the Roman numeral for one
the first word of the answer to 7 down

explanation.surface: Sugar taken from part of a tree, perhaps maple syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sugar is a British tycoon known from the TV show The Apprentice; 'Sugar maybe' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailanthus is the tree of heaven, a fast-growing ornamental genus.

clue.text: Aldi promotions initially see returns after Tesco misses out to defectors

indicators.note: after places the shortened supermarket name before the other pieces
misses out means the letters of the little word are omitted from the supermarket name

parts.note: the letters T and O

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words
returns means the word see is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before reversal

explanation.surface: Shoppers defect from Tesco to Aldi after seeing its promotions.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldi and Tesco are UK supermarkets; shoppers 'defecting' between them is the picture, while 'to' supplies the two letters Tesco loses.
explanation.definitionFit: People who escape from captivity or a regime are, like defectors, ones who have fled.

clue.text: Not friendly — while one cuts nutritional description of water

parts.note: as can mean while, at the time that

indicators.note: cuts means slicing into, so the numeral goes inside the calorie label

parts.note: water has zero calories, written 0 cal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grumpy drinker remarks on the nutrition label on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding the company of others, so not sociable or friendly.

clue.text: After change of centre spread, becomes more bare

indicators.note: change of centre means the middle letter of the word is replaced

parts.note: to scatter is to spread about

explanation.surface: After a midfield reshuffle, the spread-out team looks thinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SCATTER's middle letter T becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so the comparative form means sparser or barer.

clue.text: Passion excuse, missing start to party

indicators.note: missing start means the excuse word loses its first letter

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their passion by saying they missed the start of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, a form of passion.

clue.text: Restricted part of street magician's vanishing trick essentially, around America

indicators.note: around means the shortened name goes round the abbreviation
vanishing means that letter disappears from the magician's name

parts.note: David Blaine is an American street magician

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letter of the word trick

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A street magician's vanishing trick around America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street magician' suggests a performer; BLAINE loses I (the heart of 'trick') to make BLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane reserved for buses is a portion of the road with restricted access.

clue.text: Flo-Jo, ignoring judge, died — ugly side of runner's field?

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for judge is left out

parts.note: nickname of the American sprinter Florence Griffith-Joyner
plain means unattractive

explanation.surface: An athletics obituary for Flo-Jo, with talk of an ugly side to the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests a sprinter like Flo-Jo, but it is a river, a common crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat land beside a river that floods is literally the field at the river's side.

clue.text: See 2
Hunting call originally sets off hounds' onslaught

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A hunting call at the start sets the hounds off on their attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a cry used in hunting to point out a hare, as tally-ho is for a fox.

clue.text: Exposed rider to run with fanatical backing

parts.note: to go can mean to run, as a machine does

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: avid means keen to the point of fanaticism

explanation.surface: An exposed rider sets off at a run, cheered on by fanatical supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry, hence 'Exposed rider'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary noblewoman rode through Coventry naked, a witty way to describe her.

clue.text: See 14
One cuts off foxtrot — a losing sequence overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the run is read backwards
sequence means a run of consecutive letters from these words

explanation.surface: A dancer is cut off after a losing streak in the foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run ROTALOSI, from 'foxtrot a losing', read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolator separates one thing from others, so it is something that cuts off.

clue.text: Second date to be arranged — unknown still

indicators.note: to be arranged means the letters of date are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A second date is yet to be fixed, so the situation is still unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be arranged' turns DATE into TEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means not moving or shaking, so it is a synonym of still.
